summary.text: Stephen Otterstrom is the Democratic candidate for Utah House of Representatives District 21, an open seat with no incumbent, in the November 3, 2026 general election.

A management consultant, he won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary and said in a Ballotpedia survey that he supports a progressive income tax, funding for public education and leasing water shares for the Great Salt Lake.

paragraphs.text: Stephen Otterstrom was born in Salt Lake City, Utah, and earned a high school diploma from West High School, an associate degree from Salt Lake Community College in 2003 and a bachelor's degree from the University of Utah in 2008.
His career experience includes working as a management consultant.
Otterstrom was the runner-up in the 2025 general election for Salt Lake City Council District 1, where Victoria Petro-Eschler won with 51.8 percent of the vote to his 48.2 percent.
In 2026 he defeated Aaron Wiley in the Democratic primary for House District 21, 59.6 percent to 40.4 percent in unofficial results.
In the survey, Otterstrom said he would adopt a progressive state income tax structure to invest more in education and services for people with disabilities.
He also proposed spending about $100 million a year to lease water shares for the Great Salt Lake and promoting cooperative housing through Tenant Opportunity to Purchase legislation.
